title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false-positive match in an automated licence-plate recognition system, occurring at the point where a camera reading is escalated into a physical stop. The system flagged a plate that was not the plate it was looking for, and the alert was acted on as though it were confirmed identification. The failure sits between the sensor and the officer, in the step where a machine-generated hit is turned into an enforcement decision.

Catching it would have required independent verification of the alert before detention, which the vendor itself states should happen. The sheriff's office attributes the misread to an illegal tinted plate cover, which is a claim about the cause of the error rather than a finding about the deputy's conduct. The deputy's actions were described by the office as reasonable, and no independent determination of that is reported.

What is not established is whether the plate cover actually caused the misread, whether the alert was verified before the stop, and whether any review or consequence followed.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was detained at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy’s actions reasonable, while Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
